# `m.futures.quotes`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Quotes of futures contracts: every change of the best bid and offer.

```python
m.futures.quotes(symbols, *, venues=frozenset(dm.FuturesVenue))
```

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Contract tickers such as `"ESZ5"`, a contracts table, or `dm.ALL`. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and the rows of each one you delete leave the table. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |
| `venues` | The exchanges whose flat files `history()` reads. | The exchanges whose futures flat files `history()` reads, as a set of `dm.FuturesVenue` members: `CME`, `CBOT`, `NYMEX`, and `COMEX`; the default is all four. Massive sells futures flat files by exchange, so pass the ones your plan holds. Streams and REST reads ignore it. |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `ticker`: "The futures contract identifier, including the base symbol and contract expiration (e.g., GCJ5 for the April 2025 gold contract)."; flat files `ticker`: "The exchange symbol that this item is traded under."; WebSocket `sym`: "The ticker symbol for the given future." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Date` | String | The futures session the row belongs to (its trading date), as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: Massive's `session_end_date` from REST and the flat files. The WebSocket sends none, so a streamed row gets the session Massive's futures schedules place it in (between two sessions, the next one). A row they cannot place has a null Date, since the 17:00 Chicago rule can be wrong around a holiday, and the stream keeps running: a spread, a contract whose schedule lookup failed or did not load before the stream opened, or a row outside the loaded schedule logs a WARNING (once per product and date); a contract still being looked up (one a live watchlist or dm.ALL adds) logs at DEBUG only; a row with no readable symbol has a null Date too. From REST and flat files `session_end_date`: "Also known as the trading date, the date of the end of the trading session, in YYYY-MM-DD format." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's primary time, as an Instant. From REST and flat files `timestamp`: "The time when the quote was generated at the exchange to nanosecond precision."; WebSocket `t`: "The timestamp in Unix MS." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `BidPrice` | double | The bid price is expressed per unit of the underlying asset, and you apply the contract multiplier to get the full contract value. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `BidSize` | double | The quote size represents the number of futures contracts available at the given bid price. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `AskPrice` | double | The ask price is expressed per unit of the underlying asset, and you apply the contract multiplier to get the full contract value. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `AskSize` | double | The quote size represents the number of futures contracts available at the given ask price. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `SequenceNumber` | long | The unique sequence number assigned to this quote by the exchange. | REST, flat files |
| `ReportSequence` | long | The reporting sequence number. | REST, flat files |
| `BidTimestamp` | Instant | The time when the bid price was submitted to the exchange. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `AskTimestamp` | Instant | The time when the ask price was submitted to the exchange. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Channel` | long | The CME multicast channel this event was sourced from. | REST |
| `Exchange` | long | The exchange ID. See Exchanges (https://massive.com/docs/rest/futures/market-operations/exchanges) for Massive's mapping of exchange IDs. | flat files |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
